The fools! They thought their "analysis" could withstand the crushing weight of my legion! Even as they calculated their percentages and contemplated their meager defenses, my Shadow Legion swept across the battlefield like a dark tide. 

They saw my Shardless Agent pull at the threads of reality, and for a moment, they glimpsed the *Living End*—only for me to snatch it away! Why would I trade my glorious, living army for the dust of the graveyard when victory was already within my grasp?

With a single command, my minions—the Generous Ents, the Overlord of the Balemurk, even the lowly Street Wraith—surged forward in a final, devastating onslaught. 44 power! A cacophony of destruction that their "six permanents" could never hope to contain!

As the last of their life force flickers out, let them remember this: I am the architect of their downfall, and every card played was but a step toward their inevitable erasure! The world is mine! 

**Victory is mine!**

Additionally, casting Mishra's Bauble first and sacrificing it won't draw a card until next upkeep, so it doesn't help find a land this turn. The order matters slightly - Mox Opal should come down first as a general sequencing principle of deploying mana sources before other spells. However, since all three will likely resolve this turn with no opponent interaction possible (it's the main phase and opponent has no board), the practical impact is minimal.
